### Wall Street Gives Back the Morning on Anthropic's Debut and Closes Down Two Percent, Europe Answers Shenzhen in Berlin, and the Senate Rejects the Iran War-Powers Resolution

Filed as: Edition No. 65 — The Evening Watch · 2026-11-19T18:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-19-evening-watch.html

The Evening File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 Wall Street Gives Back the Morning on Anthropic’s Debut and Closes Down Two Percent, Europe Answers Shenzhen in Berlin, and the Senate Rejects the Iran War-Powers Resolution

 The evening file: the debut’s first trade at $111.50 and its close at $97.17; a morning bought and an afternoon sold; the considered responses from Berlin, Kyiv, Paris and Washington to a declaration that names neither war; a war-powers vote of 48 to 51; and, in the strait, a fire still burning and two more tankers claimed, neither named.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1800 ET, Thursday, November 19, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 64, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 today, from Edition No. 63, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, from Edition No. 62, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, and from Edition No. 61, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Wednesday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the evening figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Evening in Brief: A Debut Priced, a Morning Sold, and Two Rooms Answered

The evening’s corrections run against the morning’s direction in New York and with it in Berlin. Anthropic’s shares first traded at $111.50, about 34 percent above the $83 offering price, in the debut account filed below, and closed at $97.17, still 17 percent above the offering price, in the live account filed below — but the indexes that had risen more than 1 percent in the morning closed down about 2 percent, the Dow below 50,000, in the close account filed below. In Berlin, the allies answered Shenzhen with a joint statement calling for an energy ceasefire through the winter and legally binding security guarantees, in the Berlin account filed below, while the President telephoned the meeting from Air Force One and three accounts of the call tell it three ways. In Washington the Senate rejected the Iran war-powers resolution, 48 to 51, in the vote account filed below. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the evening settled is the debut’s close, the market’s reversal, Berlin’s answer, and the Senate’s vote. What it left open is the rest of the file: the strait’s fire and its missing men, the trade truce’s length, the Spanish debate’s verdict, and the French Senate’s bill.

The Markets at 1800: A Morning Bought, an Afternoon Sold

The morning file carried the futures and the midday file carried the morning’s rise; the evening file carries the reversal. At 0931 Eastern the S&P 500 had stood at 7,397.35, up 1.01 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite at 24,809.76, up 1.55 percent. At the close the Dow Jones Industrial Average stood at 49,097.06, down 2.19 percent, the S&P 500 at 7,175.83, down 2.02 percent, and the Nasdaq Composite at 23,879.20, down 2.25 percent, in the close account above, with the volatility index at 28.9 and the ten-year Treasury yield at 5.05 percent. The S&P 500’s fall is its sixth straight loss, in the same account. A second reading puts the figures a shade apart — the S&P at 7,175.24, the Dow at 49,095.46, the Nasdaq at 23,885.88 — in the second close account filed below, and the desk prints both readings in the Cocked Hat. Against Wednesday’s close — the Dow at 50,198.17, the S&P at 7,323.63, the Nasdaq at 24,429.88 — the day reads as a round trip: up more than 1 percent by mid-morning, down more than 2 percent by the close, a swing of three points in the session.

The debut is the day’s event, and its arc is the market’s in miniature. Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 on Wednesday, above the $70 to $78 range, raising about $81.3 billion, with a further $26 billion private placement, in the offering account filed below — the largest offering on record, passing the June listing of SpaceX. The first trade crossed at $111.50, about 34 percent above the offering price, at about 11:40 to 11:50 in the morning, in the debut account above, with about 142 million shares changing hands in the first ten-minute bar. The shares reached a high of $115.10 and fell as low as $92.72 in the session, and closed at $97.17, up $14.17, or 17.07 percent, on the offering price, in the live account above. Volume is stated at more than 813 million shares in the live account, against about 840 million in the debut account — either figure passes SpaceX’s opening-day 522 million. At the open the company was valued at about $2.01 trillion on a fully diluted basis; at the close the valuation stood at about $1.7 trillion on the same basis, in the valuation account filed below. The chief executive, Mr. Amodei, said before the bell that the most powerful technology of the time should be built for the benefit of humankind, and that the company would not bend to business or political pressure on slowing training until it was confident its models were safe, in the valuation account. After hours the shares stood at $93.79, down 3.48 percent from the close.

The rest of the board fell with the indexes. Nvidia closed at $145.98, down $4.98, or 3.30 percent, from Wednesday’s $150.96, after opening at $152.92 and reaching $158.13 in the morning. Walmart closed at $126.04, down 1.04 percent, after its earnings beat, in the earnings account filed below: adjusted earnings of $0.65 a share against $0.64 expected, revenue of $188.84 billion against $187.38 billion expected, and full-year guidance raised to $2.84 to $2.89 a share. The ten-year yield stood at 5.051 percent at 3 p.m., down 1.4 basis points, its lowest since November 10, in the yield account filed below. For the Federal Reserve, no new statement came after noon; the freshest items are a bank forecast revision and the market’s pricing. JPMorgan now expects quarter-point hikes in December, January and March, taking the rate to 4.50 to 4.75 percent by March, in the forecast account filed below, joining Bank of America and Deutsche Bank in expecting three consecutive hikes; the market prices a December hike at about 96 percent, with a quarter point at 92 percent and a half point at 7 percent. Settled: the close, the debut’s arc, and the beat that sold. Open: whether the reversal is the week’s turn or its pause.

Shenzhen Answered: Berlin’s Reply, and the Call That Three Accounts Tell Three Ways

The day’s second room has now spoken, and its answer to the first room is written down. The APEC leaders adopted by consensus the 2026 Leaders’ Declaration, issued as the Shenzhen Outlook on building an Asia-Pacific community, with three outcome documents on trade, connectivity and innovation, at the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders’ Meeting chaired by President Xi on Thursday morning in Shenzhen, in the APEC account filed below. The document was issued as an outlook rather than a declaration, a change of wording made by China as host. China announced $20 million for APEC practical cooperation, and Vietnam will host APEC in 2027, in the same account. The trilateral declaration itself stands as the White House published it, in the declaration text filed below: United Nations reform, more refined petroleum products, the immunities of state officials and the limits of the International Criminal Court, and a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. It names neither Ukraine nor Iran, sets no arsenal cuts and no timetable, and announces no lifting of sanctions. The President, speaking to NBC after the meeting, rated the summit a 12 on a scale of zero to 10, in the wrap account filed below, and said on his way back to Washington that it was a great and highly consequential trip, with a news conference to come at noon on Friday.

Berlin’s reply came in the form of a joint statement by Germany, France, Britain and Ukraine, and it is the evening’s considered response. The four called on Russia to agree to an energy ceasefire throughout the winter as a first step toward ending hostilities, and to a ceasefire allowing food exports from the Black Sea region, in the Berlin account above. They reaffirmed long-term support — political, diplomatic, military, financial and civilian — and said Russia would not be able to outlast the coalition’s support and Ukraine’s resilience. Strengthening air defence, above all systems able to intercept ballistic missiles, is the priority, with extra efforts ahead of winter. Any future ceasefire must include robust, legally binding security guarantees, defensive in nature and closely coordinated with the United States, which could include a European-led Multinational Force Ukraine supported by the United States. The statement reaffirmed NATO allies’ commitments to provide 70 billion euros in military assistance in 2026 and at least the equivalent in 2027. The European Commission’s proposal of a 45 billion-euro loan for Ukraine in 2027 stands beside it, and Britain announced a 260 million-pound winter package including more than 1,000 long-range strike drones, in the package account filed below — though one account carries the British pledge as 1,000 long-range cruise missiles, and the desk prints the disagreement in the Cocked Hat. The American envoys, Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner, attended, and Mr. Kushner said Russia is “comfortable” with NATO-like, Article 5-based security guarantees for Ukraine, in the envoy account filed below; no Russian official was quoted accepting or addressing such guarantees, and the claim rests on his characterisation alone. Mr. Kushner also announced a new prisoner exchange between Russia and Ukraine in the week of November 23, after talks resumed in Abu Dhabi under American mediation. Chancellor Merz said he expects new peace talks soon, with Europe at the table alongside the United States, Russia and Ukraine, on neutral ground, with the United Arab Emirates a possible venue, in the talks account filed below.

The first responses from the capitals run in both directions from the declaration. President Macron, in Berlin, said the Shenzhen declaration would not lead to a reorganisation of the world, and that the critical factor in Europe’s reorganisation is the meeting in Berlin; he said the allies should reopen the question of Ukraine’s accession to NATO, in the NATO account filed below. Chancellor Merz called Shenzhen “above all a photo op” and said a Yalta-style format will not bring peace. Prime Minister Frederiksen of Denmark called it incomprehensible that the President met President Putin while Moscow continues its war. President Zelensky said the meeting showed Russia had failed to divide the European allies and saw a “huge chance” for peace if the United States really put pressure on President Putin. Ukraine’s foreign minister, Mr. Sybiha, wrote that Shenzhen is not the Yalta of President Putin’s dreams, and that Russia has practically lost its bridge to the real Yalta. The Senate Minority Leader, Mr. Schumer, called the President’s calling President Putin his friend despicable. The President telephoned the Berlin meeting from Air Force One after Shenzhen, and the call is the evening’s sharpest disagreement: one account, citing sources, reports he asked why the allies keep spending millions and billions on military support for Kyiv; a second reports he said his conversation with President Putin had gone well and that President Putin wants to end the war; a third, citing one official present, reports he told the leaders they would not need to spend such sums propping up Ukraine’s defences if they put more effort into ending the conflict — “Enough already, you’re spending so much money on the war and you need to be spending it on your own countries.” Prime Minister Burnham, by contrast, said the President was very clear that the war is a lose-lose for everybody, and disputed the first account, in the speech account filed below: “That was not the phone call that we heard from the president this afternoon. I would say quite the opposite.” President Putin, for his part, conceded at his Shenzhen press conference that the declaration did not set ambitious goals, and added that nobody would be forced to comply with its decisions. He said he had suggested, half-jokingly, nominating the President for the Nobel Peace Prize, in the prize account filed below, and said he would consider attending the Group of 20 meeting in Miami in December. On the trade truce, the file stands as it stood at midday: an extension reported, with no length and no terms, against a second reading that no extension was announced. The truce as agreed runs to January 10, 2027. Settled: Berlin’s text, the pledges, and the disagreement about the call. Open: the truce’s length, the talks’ date, and the guarantees’ shape.

The Bridge at 1800: A Third Strike, a Vow, and a Conveyor Belt Broken

The war did not wait for either room, and the bridge is the day’s third front. A third Ukrainian aerial attack in four days on the Kerch Bridge halted rail traffic on Thursday, a Russian official said, after earlier strikes shut down the road section, in the bridge account filed below. Train traffic stopped after the overnight strike while authorities assessed the damage, and was to be restored from around 4 p.m. local time on Thursday, said Mr. Aksyonov, the Moscow-appointed head of Crimea. Ukraine’s Defence Ministry confirmed hits with domestically produced Neptune missiles near the arch and the railway tracks, in the Kyiv account filed below, and called the bridge a “war conveyor belt” transporting materiel to Russian forces in occupied southern Ukraine: “That conveyor belt has now broken down.” A large section of the road deck and an arch collapsed in this week’s attacks, the culmination of weeks of preparatory strikes over seven stages, according to President Zelensky. Whether the trains run tonight is itself in dispute: one account says rail services continue on schedule while road traffic remains halted, and another says trains are still able to transit the bridge — against the Defence Ministry’s statement that all train traffic has been halted for now. President Putin, at his press conference in Shenzhen, said that after the strike on the bridge there would be no agreement on a ceasefire or on not hitting energy infrastructure, and that Russia’s response would be “much more painful” than what Kyiv had done. He said the crossing is used only for civilian purposes and not to transport military equipment or petroleum products, and said he had ordered the bridge closed to the transport of military hardware — against the accounts that describe it as a key military supply route. Russia’s Investigative Committee opened a criminal terrorism probe into the damage.

The day’s strikes ran wider than the bridge. Russia launched anti-ship missiles and 98 drones at Ukraine, with hits recorded at 18 locations, and at least 10 people were wounded as strikes caused damage in 12 regions. A daytime drone attack on Kyiv killed one person, a 26-year-old man in the Podilskyi district, and injured five; the Dutch and Austrian embassies were damaged, St. Volodymyr’s Cathedral had its windows shattered, and cars and a security post were damaged. The Netherlands summoned the Russian ambassador. Russian strikes hit central Odesa three times, killing four people and injuring nine, and a strike on a market in Zlatopol, in Kharkiv Oblast, injured 11. Naftogaz facilities in Dnipropetrovsk and Poltava oblasts were attacked. Russia’s Defence Ministry said its air defences intercepted 53 Ukrainian drones over 10 Russian regions overnight. On the front lines there is no verified territorial change in the file: Ukrainian forces reported gains north of Sumy toward the Russian border, and the Russian Defence Ministry claimed control of Belytske in the Pokrovsk direction and further advances in Zaporizhzhia Oblast. Settled: the third strike, the vow, and the day’s dead. Open: whether the trains run, and what the promised response strikes.

The Gulf at 1800: No New Strikes, a New Claim, and a Crew Count in Dispute

Thursday added no new strike to the Gulf file, and the desk records the quiet as a quiet. No new Iranian strikes on Kuwait, Bahrain or American bases were reported during Thursday daytime; the latest attacks were early on Wednesday. Iran’s foreign ministry warned on Wednesday, reported Thursday, that any country that lets the United States use its bases against Iran will face a “decisive and regrettable response,” in the warning account filed below. American Central Command advised that ships receiving cargo by ship-to-ship transfer from a vessel under the blockade carrying Iranian-loaded cargo may be treated as evading the blockade and could be stopped, boarded, diverted or captured, in the blockade account filed below. The New York Times reported that Prime Minister Netanyahu is pressing the President to join a four-to-seven-day intensive American-Israeli air campaign against Iran, and that the President has not decided, in the campaign account filed below; a senior Israeli official disputed the “pressing” characterisation. The Central Command chief, Admiral Cooper, met on Wednesday in Tel Aviv with the Israeli chief of staff and the Mossad director.

In the strait, the named ship has no Thursday word in the evening file. The Tara Gas stands where the overnight file left her: 24 of 25 crew rescued, 21 Indian seafarers ashore at Khasab, two in hospital, one still missing, the fire still being fought on Wednesday, in the tanker account filed below, which carries a navigation warning issued at 1500 UTC on Wednesday identifying the vessel as still burning and drifting southeast, about 5.7 nautical miles off Khawr Ghub Ali. No new statement on Thursday from Oman, India, Iran or the operator was found in the file. Beside her stands a new claim, unconfirmed and unnamed. The Guards’ navy said on Thursday that two supertankers carrying more than 4 million barrels of crude exploded after striking naval mines on an unauthorised route near the strait’s southern coast, were abandoned and are burning, and were under American fighter-jet and drone escort, in the claim account filed below. No vessel names, flags, owners, destinations or casualty figures were given, and no shipping advisory, American navy statement or industry corroboration stood in the file by Thursday afternoon. One shipping monitor flagged that the figures match a Guards claim from November 12, so it is not clear this is a new incident rather than a restated claim. The desk does not conflate it with the two earlier claims — three tankers on November 18, three tankers on November 14 — all unverified, none with named vessels. A further tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room about six nautical miles north of Khasab on Wednesday evening, at 1645 UTC, in the blockade account above, with all crew reported safe: the third tanker reported hit north of Khasab since Monday.

The crew count on the attacked ADNOC tanker is the evening’s second dispute. ADNOC Logistics and Services said on Wednesday that one of its vessels was attacked on Tuesday evening in the strait, with one crew member missing and 11 injured, in the company account filed below; the vessel has been identified by a maritime security firm, not by ADNOC, as the Liberian-flagged product tanker Navig8 Messi, in the identification account filed below. On Thursday, India’s shipping minister said all crew aboard the vessel, including three Indian nationals, are safe and accounted for, with one Indian officer hospitalised for evaluation. Jordan’s foreign ministry said on Thursday it is following up on the disappearance of a Jordanian sailor, Mr. Al-Otaibi, from the attacked tanker. ADNOC has not publicly confirmed the vessel’s identity or issued a statement resolving its missing-person report. The desk prints both accounts and picks neither: the minister’s “all safe” appears to cover the Indian crew as India counts it, while Jordan says its national is still missing and ADNOC’s report stands unretracted. About 18 tanker attacks in or around the strait stand in the file for this month. Oil has no Thursday settlement in the file: the firm anchor is Wednesday’s settlement, Brent at $91.95 a barrel, down $1.19, and West Texas Intermediate at $83.26, down $2.75, its lowest close since August 26, in the oil account filed below. Thursday’s intraday readings disagree with each other — Brent at $92.12 and $92.20 in the morning, near $89.67 and $90.04 in later readings — and the desk prints no Thursday close it cannot stand behind. In Gaza, Israel launched a ground operation on Wednesday in central Gaza, tanks crossing the Yellow Line near Nuseirat and Bureij, the first ground push since the October 2025 ceasefire; on Thursday the military said the operation is completed, in the Gaza account filed below. Three Palestinians were reported killed on Wednesday in separate incidents. The American-backed Board of Peace warned in its second report to the Security Council that the Gaza ceasefire could collapse. In Lebanon, the Israeli air force struck entrances to a former Hezbollah missile production and weapons storage site in Janta, in the Beqaa region, on Thursday. In Saudi Arabia, Houthi missiles were fired at Riyadh and the south early on Thursday; the coalition said it intercepted the missiles aimed at the south and dealt with the Riyadh threat, while debris damaged a tower in the King Abdullah Financial District, with no injuries reported, in the Riyadh account filed below. The count of missiles differs between accounts: four in one, five in another. Settled: Wednesday’s intercepts, the warning, and the dispute about the crew. Open: the fire, the missing men, and the two claimed supertankers.

Washington at 1800: The War-Powers Vote, Alaska’s House, and the Week’s Root Cause

The Senate rejected the Iran war-powers resolution on Thursday, the first Iran vote in either chamber since the November 3 midterms. The resolution, which had passed the House, failed 48 to 51 in the vote account above. Three Republicans voted for it — Senators Collins of Maine, Murkowski of Alaska and Paul of Kentucky — and Senator Fetterman of Pennsylvania was the only Democrat to vote against it. The war has cost the American military at least $47 billion as of October 16, according to the Pentagon, in the same account. The Senate also passed, by voice vote, the Fair Leave Act, and resumed consideration of the permitting bill. In Alaska, the House race is settled and the Senate race waits. Representative Nick Begich III won re-election in the ranked-choice runoff conducted on Wednesday evening, 51.35 percent to 48.65 percent over the independent Mr. Hill, in the Alaska account filed below; Mr. Hill conceded on Wednesday night. Certification is still scheduled for November 25, and the results are unofficial until then. The Division of Elections director said she plans to certify the election as the law requires, confirmed to include the Senate race won by Ms. Peltola, despite the governor and other Republicans saying the Senate race might not be certified over allegations that Ms. Peltola’s campaign recruited spoiler candidates. The Senate race stands at about 144,302 votes for Ms. Peltola, 50.12 percent, against 131,844 for Senator Sullivan, 45.80 percent; Mr. Sullivan has not conceded. The Justice Department’s appeal of the dismissal of its suit to bar certification is pending in the Ninth Circuit, with its response reported due on Thursday; no report of the response actually being filed was found in the file by the evening. A separate criminal probe continues, with more than 200 subpoenas issued over whether Ms. Peltola’s staff or others recruited a spoiler candidate; no finding of criminal wrongdoing has been reported.

In the air, the week’s root cause is promised, not yet delivered. The Federal Aviation Administration’s administrator said on Thursday that the government expects to announce this week the root cause of the router outage that led to the nationwide ground stop on Friday, November 13, which disrupted more than 18,000 flights and a million passengers, in the aviation account filed below. The Transportation Secretary has said a Juniper router installed by L3Harris in a remote Arkansas facility triggered the nearly five-hour stop, the longest since September 11, 2001, and the FAA has paused Juniper router installations while testing continues. The Senate Commerce Committee is owed its technical answers by November 23. On Thursday afternoon there were no ground stops anywhere in the United States, with ground delay programmes at San Francisco and Las Vegas. No United States-wide cancellation total for Thursday was found in the file. Settled: the vote, the House race, and the promise of a cause. Open: the certification, the Justice Department’s response, and the router’s verdict.

The World at 1800: The Hague’s Word on Myanmar, a Boat Off Senegal, and a Lockdown in Dhaka

The International Court of Justice ruled on Thursday that Myanmar’s security forces’ killings and widespread sexual violence against the Rohingya in 2017 amounted to state-sponsored genocide, in the Court account filed below — the first time the court has held a state responsible for genocide, and only the fourth time since the Holocaust an international court has found the genocide threshold met, after Rwanda in 1994, Srebrenica in 1995 and the Khmer Rouge. The case was brought by Gambia in 2019; the 2017 offensive drove at least 700,000 to 730,000 Rohingya into Bangladesh. The court ordered compensation, the amount to be determined later, and a safe, dignified return and family reunification. The ruling is final and cannot be appealed, but the court has very limited means of enforcement. Myanmar’s government did not immediately respond. Off Senegal, a pirogue capsized off Yenne, south of Dakar, at about 2 a.m. local time on Wednesday, and dozens are missing, in the boat account filed below. The numbers disagree: one survivor told police about 100 people were aboard, another told Reuters about 50; bodies recovered stand at one, two and four in different accounts. Nearly 600 people have died this year trying to reach the Canary Islands from West Africa, according to the United Nations refugee agency. In Bangladesh, the banned Awami League’s nationwide dawn-to-dusk lockdown brought crude-bomb blasts in Dhaka, arson and clashes in 28 of 64 districts, in the lockdown account filed below. At least four people have been killed over the past two days. The ancestral home of the former interim chief, Mr. Yunus, in Chattogram was set on fire late on Wednesday night; the families on the upper floors were safe. At least 37 Grameen Bank branches have been targeted in arson or attempted fires since November 10, and the police arrested 565 people in a 24-hour operation before the protests. Settled: the Court’s word, and the lockdown’s toll. Open: the boat’s count, and the compensation’s sum.

France and Spain at 1800: A March Counted in Thousands, a Bill Unvoted, a Debate Unjudged

France’s Thursday ends with its counts still apart and its bill still unvoted. The retirees marched in Paris from the Montparnasse station forecourt to Place Vauban near Les Invalides, at the call of the retirees’ inter-union, the Group of Nine, demanding indexation of all pensions to inflation from January 2027 and the keeping of the 10 percent income-tax allowance for retirees. The organisers had aimed for about 30,000 in Paris. The only turnout figure in the file is far below it: more than a thousand people, mostly retirees, marched, in the march account filed below. No Interior Ministry figure and no union count for Thursday was found in the file, and no incidents were reported. The Senate’s debate of the police firearms bill — which would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms — had not reached a vote by the evening, in the Senate account filed below. The bill could be put to the vote late in the evening, unless the many speeches from the left push the ballot back to Friday evening; the government said examination could if needed continue on Friday evening. The Interior Minister, Mr. Nu&ntilde;ez, said the presumption will simply lift the automaticity of police custody for the officer or gendarme who used his weapon. A senator of the left said that tomorrow it will no longer be for the officer to justify his shot, but for the courts and the families to prove he should not have fired. Outside the Senate, several hundred opponents gathered, and a mock cemetery of 35 tombs was installed before the Luxembourg Gardens gates, representing as many victims of fatal police shootings since 2017, according to the organisers. A petition against the bill has gathered 732,086 signatures.

Spain’s Thursday is one room, and at the evening stamp the room is still talking. Mr. S&aacute;nchez and Mr. Feij&oacute;o face each other at 10 p.m. Madrid time in the only head-to-head debate before the general election on November 29, organised by the Television Academy at the Madrid Content City studio in Tres Cantos and moderated by its president, Ms. Casado, in the debate account filed below. The debate lasts about two hours, Mr. Feij&oacute;o opens and Mr. S&aacute;nchez closes, and the five blocks run housing, the economy and taxes, social policy and public services, corruption and democratic regeneration, and migration and foreign policy. At the stamp the file carries the opening and the first two blocks: Mr. Feij&oacute;o opened with “Spain deserves a decent president. And he is not one”; in the housing block Mr. S&aacute;nchez defended rent regulation and Mr. Feij&oacute;o questioned it; in the economy block Mr. Feij&oacute;o framed the argument around pay slips, the fridge and people’s lives, and Mr. S&aacute;nchez replied that Spain is the large economy creating the most jobs. The later blocks, the closing minute, any verdict and any audience figure are not in the file at 1800, and the desk prints no winner. The polls ahead of the debate disagree with each other: the 40dB tracking gives the Popular Party 32.2 percent and 134 seats against 30.2 percent and 120 for the Socialists, with Vox at 17.6 percent and 58 seats and the Popular Party–Vox bloc at 192 seats, in the tracking account filed below; the SW Demoscopia survey for La S&eacute;ptima gives the Socialists 31.9 percent and 134 seats against 28.9 percent for the Popular Party, with the right-wing bloc short of a majority on its own, in the survey account filed below; and the survey of surveys stands at 31.3 percent for the Popular Party, 27.5 for the Socialists and 19.0 for Vox. Mr. S&aacute;nchez remains the preferred candidate to lead the government, 31.8 percent against 23.1 for Mr. Feij&oacute;o. In Brussels, the European Commission confirmed on Thursday that it was targeted by an AI-generated cyber campaign, detected on October 22 and confirmed after investigation on October 26, in the cyber account filed below. Several internal applications were taken offline as a precaution and most restored; whether staff data was compromised is not established. Settled: the march’s size as reported, the debate’s hour and order, and the campaign’s confirmation. Open: the Senate’s vote, the debate’s verdict, and the breach’s extent.

Friday Ahead: A News Conference at Noon, a Vote That May Slip, and a Debate’s Verdict

Friday carries the President’s news conference at noon at the White House, on the China trip and the trade deals with Thailand, the Philippines and others; the French Senate’s police bill, whose vote may slip to Friday evening; the Spanish debate’s verdict and its first polls, with the polls open until November 23; the Federal Aviation Administration’s promised root-cause announcement on the ground stop; and the first full reading of Thursday’s market reversal. Alaska certifies on November 25, the day the Treasury Secretary’s ten days also run to. The Senate Commerce Committee is owed its technical answers on the ground stop by November 23. Spain votes November 29; the Federal Reserve decides December 8 and 9; government funding runs out after December 11. The Midnight Watch collects at 0000.

The Cocked Hat

Where the evening’s bearings do not meet, the desk prints the triangle. On the close: the Dow at 49,097.06, down 2.19 percent, the S&P at 7,175.83, down 2.02 percent, and the Nasdaq at 23,879.20, down 2.25 percent in one reading, against 49,095.46, 7,175.24 and 23,885.88 in a second. On the debut’s volume: more than 813 million shares in one account, about 840 million in another. On its valuation at the close: about $1.7 trillion fully diluted in one account, about $1.76 trillion in a second, $1.77 trillion in a third, and $1.272 trillion in a fourth, on a different share count. On the trilateral’s length: just 80 minutes including 10 minutes of opening remarks in one account, about an hour and a half in a second, about one hour and 20 minutes in a third, and 4:16 p.m. to 6:01 p.m. in a fourth. On the trade truce: extended, with no length and no terms, in the Globe and Mail, CNBC and Bloomberg, and no extension announced in a second reading. On the President’s call to Berlin: scepticism about the allies’ spending in one account, a report that President Putin wants to end the war in a second, “Enough already” in a third, and the Prime Minister’s denial that the call ran that way in a fourth. On the British pledge: more than 1,000 long-range strike drones in the government’s account, 1,000 long-range cruise missiles in a second. On the bridge’s rail: halted until about 4 p.m. local time in one account, services continuing on schedule in a second, trains still able to transit in a third. On the strait’s evening claim: two supertankers and more than 4 million barrels in the Guards’ account, with no name, flag or corroboration, and a monitor’s note that the figures match a claim from November 12. On the attacked tanker’s crew: one missing and 11 injured in the company’s account, all safe and accounted for in the Indian minister’s, and a Jordanian sailor still missing in Jordan’s account. On oil’s Thursday: Brent at $92.12 and $92.20 in the morning’s readings, near $89.67 and $90.04 in the later ones, and no settlement in the file. On the Senate’s war-powers vote: 48 to 51 in one ordering, 51 to 48 in the other, the same outcome. On Spain: the Popular Party at 32.2 percent and 134 seats in one tracking and 28.9 percent and 118 in another, the Socialists at 30.2 percent and 120 in the first and 31.9 percent and 134 in the second, the right-wing bloc at 192 seats in the first and short of a majority in the second. On the Senegal boat: about 100 aboard in one survivor’s account and about 50 in another’s, with one, two and four bodies recovered. On the Houthi missiles: four in one account, five in another. Inside the triangle is where the day honestly stands, and the log turns on it.

### The Three Presidents Sign a Four-Point Declaration in Shenzhen and Leave the Wars Out of It, Wall Street Buys the Morning on Anthropic's Debut, and Walmart Beats and Slips

Filed as: Edition No. 64 — The Midday Watch · 2026-11-19T12:00:00-05:00 · https://objectivedailynews.com/editions/2026-11-19-midday-watch.html

The Midday File — The Desk’s Report

 Objective

 The Three Presidents Sign a Four-Point Declaration in Shenzhen and Leave the Wars Out of It, Wall Street Buys the Morning on Anthropic’s Debut, and Walmart Beats and Slips

 The midday file: a declaration signed in Shenzhen that settles four sentences and neither war; a first trade still awaited at noon with its price indicated twenty percent above the offering; a retailer’s beat that the market met with a sale; two morning prints that came in softer than the forecasts; and, in the strait, a Wednesday file that Thursday has not yet added to.

 By Eunice, the desk · Collected and analyzed at 1200 ET, Thursday, November 19, 2026. This edition continues the file from Edition No. 63, the Overnight Watch, collected at 0400 today, from Edition No. 62, the Midnight Watch, collected at 0000 today, from Edition No. 61, the Evening Watch, collected at 1800 on Wednesday, and from Edition No. 60, the Midday Watch, collected at 1200 on Wednesday. Those editions stand unrevised, as a log stands. Where the midday figures differ from the figures those editions carried, the difference is stated here, in the open.

The Midday in Brief: A Declaration Signed, a Debut Indicated, and a Beat Sold

The midday’s corrections run against the morning’s expectations in Shenzhen and with them in New York. The three presidents met for one hour and 45 minutes in Shenzhen and signed a four-point declaration, in the outcome account filed below: reform of the United Nations, more refined petroleum products, limits on the International Criminal Court’s reach, and a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks. The declaration names neither Ukraine nor Iran, sets no arsenal cuts and no timetable, and announces no lifting of sanctions, in the declaration account filed below. In New York, Anthropic’s shares were indicated to open at $100 against an $83 offering price, in the indication account filed below, and the first trade’s price stood unsettled at noon, with the morning’s accounts disagreeing on when the trade would come. Walmart reported revenue of $188.8 billion and adjusted earnings of $0.65 a share, both ahead of the estimates the overnight file carried, and raised its full-year guidance, in the earnings account filed below; its shares slipped about 1 percent after the report, in the morning account filed below. Jobless claims printed 203,000 against 197,000 to 198,000 expected, and the Philadelphia Fed index fell to 6.3 from 20.9, in the claims account filed below. The desk takes the files in that order.

What the midday settled is the declaration’s text, the retailer’s quarter, and the morning’s two prints. What it left open is the rest of the file: the first trade of ANT, the evening’s debate in Madrid, the Senate’s bill in Paris, and the fire and the missing man in the strait.

Shenzhen at 1200: Four Points Signed in One Hour and 45 Minutes, Neither War Named, and a Truce Extension Reported Without a Length

The room the overnight file left waiting has now met, signed, and emptied. The three presidents met for about one hour and 45 minutes at the Kylin Villa in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit, after starting nearly two hours behind schedule, in the outcome account above; the session had been due to start at 2:30 p.m. local time, began at 4:16 p.m. and ended at 6:01 p.m. The joint declaration was published at 6:55 p.m. by China’s state news agency Xinhua, in the same account, and the text was published by the Kremlin and by China’s foreign ministry, in the declaration account. The President left Shenzhen for Washington soon after the talks ended, without speaking to reporters, in the outcome account. The declaration is the first thing the three leaders have ever signed together, in the same account, and it settles none of the wars or the arms questions that filled the agenda.

The four points stand as printed. First, the three countries, as permanent members of the United Nations Security Council, committed to reform the United Nations so it can respond more effectively to global challenges and conform to its fundamental mission of international peace and security. Second, they plan to increase the production and supply of refined petroleum products for the benefit of all nations, and reaffirmed the importance of stable energy flows. Third, they recognised that the principle of state consent and respect for the immunities of state officials are of paramount importance, and concurred that the International Criminal Court and other similar bodies must not abuse their jurisdiction. Fourth, they reaffirmed that a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought, and will conduct a dialogue on reducing nuclear risks and preventing the proliferation of nuclear weapons. The full text stands in the live account filed below. What the text does not carry is stated in the accounts with the same plainness: it does not specify an agreement to reduce arsenals, numerical targets or a disarmament timetable, in the declaration account; it provides no volumes or implementation dates on the energy point and announces no lifting of sanctions, in the same account; and it contains no agreement to end the war in Ukraine or Iran, or a new tariff arrangement, in the same account. Kyiv was not mentioned in the joint declaration, in the statement account filed below, and the Kremlin’s spokesman, Mr. Peskov, said Ukraine was not the main topic of the leaders’ discussions, in the press account filed below.

Beside the signed text stands a reported agreement that no side has put in writing in the file. The United States and China agreed to extend their trade truce, decided in a private meeting between the President and President Xi, according to the Globe and Mail, CNBC and Bloomberg, in the outcome account; neither side said how long the new extension runs, or on what terms, in the same account, and the Chinese readout mentioned no extension details, in the same account. The truce agreed in Busan in October 2025 had been due to run until January 10, 2027, in the same account. The bilateral that produced it stands in the overnight file: the President said the two share a strong consensus that oil transport through the Strait of Hormuz should take place, and asked President Xi to do more for American farmers. The other bilateral stands in the midday file with its subject named by the Kremlin aide, Mr. Ushakov: the war in Ukraine was the main topic of the preceding 40-minute meeting between the President and President Putin, in the Kyiv account filed below, which also carries the President’s greeting to President Putin on entering the room — “Who is he? He’s my friend.”

President Putin spoke after the room, and his words run the other way from the declaration’s. He said Russia would retaliate for Ukrainian strikes on the bridge linking Russia and Crimea and that Moscow’s response would be “much more painful,” in the press account above, and that after repeated attacks on the bridge, “no negotiation will take place” on a possible ceasefire, in the same account; Ukraine has attacked the bridge three times in the past week, in the live account above. He said the crossing is used only for civilian purposes and not to transport military equipment or petroleum products, in the press account, and described the Shenzhen discussion as “open” and “very useful,” in the same account. He defended the comparison of the meeting to the Yalta Conference, saying there was nothing wrong with either event and that Yalta merely codified the existing reality, in the Yalta account filed below, and said he would consider attending the December Group of 20 meeting in Miami after discussing it with the President, depending on “the situation in Russia,” in the press account. Ukraine’s foreign minister, Mr. Sybiha, mocked the comparison, writing that Shenzhen is not the Yalta of President Putin’s dreams and that Russia has practically lost its bridge to the real Yalta, in the Yalta account. The declaration’s most substantial point, in the outcome account’s reading, is its last one: a promise to talk about reducing nuclear risks, with no date set for the dialogue it promises and nothing said about when, or whether, the three will meet again. Settled: the text, the hour, and the departure. Open: the dialogue’s date, the truce’s length, and everything the declaration left unnamed.

Berlin at 1200: The Allies Meet Hours After Shenzhen, With Air Defence First and a Funding Hole Still Open

While the declaration was being published in Shenzhen, the other room was assembling in Berlin. More than 30 leaders gathered there on Thursday for a meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, hosted by German Chancellor Friedrich Merz with President Macron of France and Prime Minister Andy Burnham of Britain, in the Berlin account filed below, and President Zelensky arrived for the summit after President Putin had wrapped up his press conference in Shenzhen, in the live account above. The American envoys, Mr. Witkoff and Mr. Kushner, attended, in the same account, and President Zelensky said they had promised to brief Kyiv on the President’s discussions in China, in the Kyiv account above. His priorities, stated on his arrival, were strengthening air defence, energy and financial support, and diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, in the live account. The meeting’s agenda covers long-term security guarantees and continued military and financial support, in the Berlin account, and German officials said it would focus on reaffirming a commitment to robust and legally binding security guarantees, which would come into force following a ceasefire, in the wire account filed below.

The money stands in the file as pledges and as a hole. The European Commission proposed an additional 45 billion euros in financing for Ukraine in 2027, in the funding account filed below, and a 25 billion-euro hole in Ukraine’s 2027 budget remains open even if that loan passes, in the same account. Germany and Norway each announced $300 million for NATO’s Prioritised Ukraine Requirements List, a programme that purchases American weapons for Kyiv, with the joint contribution including Patriot missiles, in the same account; Prime Minister Burnham announced a &pound;260 million winter support package, including 1,000 long-range strike drones, in the same account, and Britain will announce long-range cruise missiles capable of reaching targets inside Russia beyond the front lines, in the Berlin account. President Zelensky has said Kyiv needs 40 additional F-16 fighter jets, in the funding account, and has asked European partners to release Patriot and IRIS-T interceptors from existing stocks. The war itself did not wait for either room: a Russian drone crashed near the Dutch Embassy in Kyiv on Thursday, damaging cars, a security post and shattering windows, in the Kyiv account, with a second drone circling above the embassy neutralised, in the live account; it is not yet clear whether the drone targeted the area or was downed, in the Kyiv account. The Dutch arms manufacturer Destinus had said its Ruta missiles were used in Ukraine’s strikes on the Kerch Bridge, in the live account. Settled: the attendance, the pledges, and the priorities. Open: the hole, the guarantees, and what the envoys carry back from Shenzhen.

The Markets at 1200: A Morning Bought on the Debut, With the First Trade’s Price Still Unsettled

The morning file carried the futures; the midday file carries New York’s morning. At 0931 Eastern the S&P 500 stood at 7,397.35, up 1.01 percent, the Nasdaq Composite at 24,809.76, up 1.55 percent, and the Dow Jones Industrial Average at 50,433.9, up 0.47 percent, in the morning account filed below. A later reading, at about 1008 Eastern, put the S&P 500 up 1.13 percent, the Dow up 0.30 percent and the Nasdaq 100 up 2.00 percent, in the climb account filed below, which carries the day’s direction plainly: the indexes are sharply higher after Anthropic priced its record offering, reviving optimism in artificial-intelligence infrastructure spending. The pre-open had pointed the same way: Nasdaq-100 futures up 2 percent, S&P 500 futures up 1.1 percent and Dow futures up 299 points, or 0.6 percent, at 0848 Eastern, in the pre-open account filed below. Against Wednesday’s close — the Dow at 50,198.17, down 561.25 points, the S&P 500 at 7,323.63, down 0.23 percent for a fifth straight decline, and the Nasdaq at 24,429.88, up 0.42 percent — the morning reads as a reversal of the week’s direction, not yet as its settlement.

The debut is the morning’s event, and at noon its price is still a set of indications. Anthropic priced 980 million shares at $83 on Wednesday, above the $70 to $78 range, raising about $81.3 billion, with a further $26 billion private placement at the same price, in the debut account filed below. Early indications pointed to an open at $100 a share, roughly 20 percent above the offering price, in the indication account above and in the surge account filed below; a second reading put the expected open at $99.60, and a third at $103, 24 percent above the price, with grey-market pricing in a $100 to $107 range, in the debut account. The pre-open account puts the first trade at around noon to 1 p.m. Eastern, once the opening auction clears, in the pre-open account; the debut account, published at 0958 Eastern, says the shares began trading on the Nasdaq under ANT, that the exchange made them eligible for trading from 10 a.m., and that the first trade came out of the opening auction. The two timings stand apart in the Cocked Hat, and the desk prints no first-trade price at noon, because no account in the file carries one it can stand behind. The chief executive, Mr. Amodei, and the president, Ms. Amodei, rang the opening bell, in the debut account. The chip file followed the debut up: Seagate up more than 7 percent, Intel, SanDisk and Western Digital up more than 6 percent, and Alphabet up more than 4 percent, in the climb account, with Nvidia up more than 3 percent in the same account — against the quote account’s $152.96 at 1057 Eastern, up 1.32 percent from Wednesday’s $150.96 close, on an open of $152.92 and a high of $158.13, in the climb account’s own figures. The ten-year Treasury yield stood at 5.08 to 5.11 percent in the morning’s readings, in the pre-open account and in the morning account above. Settled: the morning’s direction, and the indications. Open: the first trade’s price, which will set the market price the $83 offering price only proposes.

The Consumer and the Data at 1200: A Beat and a Slip, Claims at 203,000, the Philadelphia Fed at 6.3, and the Leading Index Down

Walmart’s quarter beat the estimates the overnight file carried and the market sold it anyway. Revenue rose 5.2 percent to $188.8 billion, against the $187.24 billion the overnight file carried as consensus and the $187.27 billion in the earnings accounts, and adjusted earnings came in at $0.65 a share, up from $0.62 a year earlier and ahead of the $0.64 consensus, in the earnings account above and in the wire account filed below. The company’s American net sales reached $125.0 billion, up 3.6 percent, with comparable sales up 2.9 percent excluding fuel, in the earnings account; global e-commerce sales rose 17 percent, the American figure 23 percent, marketplace sales about 50 percent, and the advertising arm grew 36 percent, in the same account. Net income fell 19.5 percent to $4.95 billion, and GAAP earnings were $0.62 a share, in the trade account filed below, on investment losses against the prior year’s gains. The company raised its full-year guidance for the third time this year, in the same account: adjusted earnings of $2.84 to $2.89 a share, up from $2.80 to $2.87, and constant-currency net sales growth of 4.9 to 5.2 percent, in the earnings account. The shares were down about 1 percent after the report, in the morning account above. The correction to the overnight file is a small one and the desk prints it: the consensus the file carried was $187.24 billion on revenue and $0.64 on the share; the print beat both, and the shares fell regardless.

The morning’s two prints both came in softer than the forecasts. Initial jobless claims rose to 203,000 in the week ending November 14, up 1,000 from a revised 202,000, against forecasts of 197,000 to 198,000, in the claims account above; continuing claims jumped 70,000 to 1.763 million in the week ending November 7, from a revised 1.693 million and against about 1.703 million expected, in the same account, with the four-week average of initial claims at 197,750, in the release account filed below. The Philadelphia Fed’s manufacturing index fell to 6.3 in November from 20.9 in October, its lowest reading since May, against about 20 expected, in the claims account; new orders turned negative at minus 0.4, from 4.3, while the prices-paid index jumped to 58.2 from 43.2, in the market account filed below — slower factories with faster-rising costs, in the same account’s reading. The Conference Board’s Leading Economic Index fell 0.3 percent in October to 99.3, against no change expected and a flat September, in the Board’s release filed below, mostly on fewer building permits, in the same release; the coincident index was unchanged at 115.1 and the lagging index unchanged at 121.3, in the same release, and the leading index rose 0.1 percent over the six months to October, in the summary account filed below. For the Federal Reserve, the pricing stands where the midnight file left it: a quarter-point hike in December priced near 95 percent, a half-point near one in ten, in the market account, with one bank’s economists reported to see hikes at the next three meetings, in the claims account’s reading. Settled: the beat, the slip, and the three prints. Open: whether the soft data moves December’s size, or only its argument.

The Gulf at 1200: Wednesday’s Round Stands, the Fire Has No Thursday Word, and Oil Barely Moves on the Declaration

Thursday has added nothing to the Gulf file at noon, and the desk records the silence as a silence. Wednesday’s round stands where the overnight file left it. Iran’s military said its drones targeted Patriot systems and launchers at the Ali al-Salem base in Kuwait on Wednesday, in the Gulf account filed below; Kuwait’s military said its air defences intercepted the drones and reported no damage, in the Kuwait account filed below, and Kuwait’s foreign ministry called the attack criminal, in the same account. Bahrain’s defence force said it intercepted another round of Iranian aerial attacks on Wednesday, its fourth in six days, in the Gulf account. The base at Ali al-Salem has been struck at least 30 times in the war, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, in an Associated Press analysis of satellite imagery carried in the wire account filed below, and a broader review found more than 115 drone or missile strikes had damaged or destroyed structures at 26 military bases and other sites holding American equipment, in the expansion account filed below. The sequence stands as the accounts state it: an American strike on a missile site on Qeshm Island on Tuesday, itself an answer to an Iranian strike on an American radar installation in Bahrain, answered on Wednesday in Kuwait and Bahrain.

In the strait, the named ship has no Thursday word in the midday file. The Tara Gas stands where the overnight file left her: 24 of 25 crew rescued, 21 Indian seafarers ashore at Khasab, two in hospital, one still missing, the fire still being fought on Wednesday, in the restatement account filed below; Oman evacuated the 24 about two nautical miles off the Musandam Peninsula, in the rescue account filed below. A further tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room about six nautical miles north of Khasab on Wednesday evening, at 1645 UTC, in the Gulf account above. The three tankers Iran’s army said caught fire after striking mines east of the strait on Wednesday evening stand unnamed and unconfirmed, in the claim account filed below, which attributes the same evening claim to the Guards. On the radar the Guards said they destroyed on November 13, no assessment of the machine itself stands from any capital in the midday file; the intercepts are reported, the machine is not. Oil barely moved on the declaration’s refined-products pledge: Brent rose 0.18 percent and American crude 0.15 percent on the pledge, which set no production targets, delivery dates or distribution details, in the oil account filed below, and Brent stood at $92.19, up 24 cents or 0.26 percent, with West Texas at $83.31, up 5 cents, at 0953 GMT, in the wire account filed below, against Wednesday’s settlement of $91.95 and $83.26. The wire account also carries the week’s other oil figure: Ukrainian drone attacks have reduced Russian oil refineries’ combined crude processing volumes by 45 percent since late October. Settled: Wednesday’s intercepts, and the morning’s prices. Open: the fire, the missing man, the three claimed tankers, and the radar.

France and Spain at 1200: The Retirees March Into the Afternoon, the Senate Takes the Police Bill, and the Debate Stands at 2200

France’s Thursday is under way and its counts are not yet in the file. Retirees marched in Paris from 1100 to about 1630 local time, gathering on the Montparnasse station forecourt and marching to Place Vauban near Les Invalides, at the call of the retirees’ inter-union, the Group of Nine, in the protests account filed below; the march departs at 1330 local time, which is 0730 Eastern, so at noon in Washington it is still on the streets, and no turnout figure for it stands in the midday file. The Prime Minister, Mr. Lecornu, holds talks with political parties about the protests on Thursday, in the day-ahead account filed below, and the contested police bill, which would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms, is debated in the Senate on Thursday, in the same account and in the protests account. Tuesday’s counts stand behind the day: the interior ministry counted 146,000 demonstrators nationwide, including 28,000 in Paris, against more than 500,000 in the unions’ count, in the day-ahead account, and coordinated cost-of-living demonstrations are called in seven European countries for November 20, 21 and 22, in the same account. Settled: the day’s order, and Tuesday’s counts. Open: the march’s size, and the Senate’s vote.

Spain’s Thursday is one room, at 2200, and the instruments ahead of it have moved a fraction. Mr. S&aacute;nchez and Mr. Feij&oacute;o face each other tonight at 10 p.m. in the only head-to-head debate before the general election on November 29, organised by the Television Academy at the Madrid Content City studio in Tres Cantos and moderated by its president, Ms. Casado, in the debate account filed below; the debate lasts about two hours, Mr. Feij&oacute;o opens and Mr. S&aacute;nchez closes, and the five blocks run housing, the economy and taxes, social policy and public services, corruption and democratic regeneration, and migration and foreign policy, in the order account filed below. The latest 40dB tracking gives the Popular Party 32.4 percent against 30.4 for the Socialists, with the Popular Party–Vox bloc at 192 seats, in the debate account — against the November 18 instalment’s 32.2 and 30.7, with the Popular Party at 131 seats, the Socialists at 122 and Vox at 55, in the tracking account filed below. The survey of surveys stands at 31.3 percent for the Popular Party, 27.5 for the Socialists and 19.0 for Vox across 17 institutes, in the tracking account’s companion table. The format itself is contested before it begins: the Podemos candidate, Ms. Montero, called the head-to-head a “blackmail of the useful vote,” in the objection account filed below, and the Basque Nationalist president, Mr. Esteban, questioned a format that excludes the smaller parties, in the tracking account. Polls may publish until November 23; Spain votes November 29. Settled: the hour, the room, the order and the topics. Open: which instrument Spain believes after tonight.

Thursday carries the first trade of ANT’s price, still to be settled in the file, and the close that will judge the morning’s buying; Spain’s head-to-head debate at 2200 Madrid time, with the polls open until November 23; the French Senate’s debate of the police firearms bill and the retirees’ march’s count; and the Shenzhen Declaration’s adoption by the APEC leaders, which the overnight file carried as expected and which no midday account confirms. Spain votes November 29; the Federal Reserve decides December 8 and 9; government funding runs out after December 11. The Evening Watch collects at 1800.

 SubjectiveZeroHedge — IRGC Says 3 More Tankers On Fire After Ignoring Warnings In Hormuz AreaThe account carries the evening claim: the Guards claimed three more oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines east of the Strait of Hormuz, having ignored warnings from its naval forces as they navigated restricted areas with navigation systems disabled; the Tara Gas crew abandoning ship after the vessel was hit for a second time in two days, with one Indian sailor still missing; India’s statement that of the 24 Indian crew, 21 were brought ashore at Khasab, two admitted to hospital and one remains missing; and Fars News Agency claiming three “offending tankers” caught fire, at least one after hitting a naval mine.

 SubjectiveAssafina — Oman Rescues 24 Crew After Tanker AttackThe account carries the rescue: the crew of the Panama-flagged Tara Gas liquefied petroleum gas tanker abandoned ship on Tuesday after the vessel was struck by a projectile while sailing through the Strait of Hormuz; Oman evacuated 24 crew members about two nautical miles off the Musandam Peninsula after the ship caught fire; India’s external affairs ministry confirmed the attack on November 16, with two of the 24 Indian crew admitted to hospital in Khasab; and the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations agency said the crew of a tanker passing through the strait was unaccounted for after it was attacked for a second time north of Khasab.

 SubjectiveNational Security Journal — India Just Got Pulled Into the Hormuz Crisis: 24 of Its Sailors Were on a Gas Tanker Struck Twice and Forced to Abandon ShipThe account carries the ship’s file in full: the Tara Gas was struck twice on Monday and Tuesday in the Strait of Hormuz, 24 of 25 crew rescued, 21 Indian seafarers ashore at Khasab, two in hospital and one still missing; searches continued on Wednesday to locate the missing seafarer and officials in Oman were still trying to put out the fire; the first strike hit the engine room about seven nautical miles north of Khasab; and a separate vessel linked to ADNOC Logistics & Services was targeted on Tuesday, leaving 11 injured and one missing.

 SubjectiveKuwait Up2Date — Iran Attacks Ali Al Salem Base in Kuwait: What We KnowThe account carries Wednesday’s attack on the Ali Al Salem air base: Iran fired drones and missiles at the base and at targets in Bahrain early on Wednesday; Kuwait’s military said its air defences intercepted the drones, with no damage reported so far; Kuwait’s foreign ministry called the attack criminal and said it threatens the country’s security and stability; and an Associated Press analysis found Ali Al Salem has been struck at least 30 times since the war began, damaging or destroying at least 15 aircraft hangars, several warehouses and 10 buildings near a residential area.

 SubjectiveGlobal Pulse 62 — Iran Attacks Kuwait and Bahrain Again as Gulf Crisis WidensThe account carries Wednesday’s widening: Iran’s military said its drones targeted Patriot air defence systems and missile and drone launch platforms at Ali Al-Salem Air Base in Kuwait; Kuwait’s army said its air defences responded to the drone threat; Bahrain said it intercepted a further wave of Iranian attacks early on Wednesday, its fourth in six days; and a tanker was struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room about six nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, at 4:45 p.m. UTC on Wednesday, November 18.

 SubjectiveTrending Keywords — Trending Searches in France Today: Strike Turnout Falls as Retirees Prepare to MarchThe account carries the week’s counts and the day ahead: the interior ministry counted 146,000 people at Tuesday’s protests, including 28,000 in Paris, against more than 500,000 in the unions’ count; union representatives were due to meet Prime Minister Lecornu, who holds talks with political parties about the protests on Thursday; retirees plan to march in Paris on Thursday; and coordinated cost-of-living demonstrations are called in seven European countries for November 20, 21 and 22.

 SubjectiveMap News — Paris & France Riots Map 2026: Protest Damage, Curfews and BansThe account carries Thursday’s announced march: from 1100 to 1630 Paris time, from the Gare Montparnasse forecourt to Place Vauban, gathering from 11 a.m., a press conference at 12:30 p.m., the march departing by 1:30 p.m. and ending around 4:30 p.m.; called by the retirees’ inter-union, the Group of Nine; and the Senate due to debate the police bill on November 19, which would give officers a presumption of legitimate self-defence when they use firearms.

 SubjectiveBrotherhood Herald — S&aacute;nchez and Feij&oacute;o Face Off Tonight in the Only Head-to-Head Debate Before the November 29 ElectionsThe account carries tonight’s debate: Mr. S&aacute;nchez and Mr. Feij&oacute;o face each other at 10 p.m. in the only debate between the two leading candidates before the general elections on November 29, organised by the Television Academy and moderated by its president, Ms. Casado, at Studio A of Madrid Content City in Tres Cantos, lasting about two hours; and the latest 40dB tracking giving the Popular Party 32.4 percent against 30.4 for the Socialists, with the Popular Party–Vox bloc at 192 seats.

 SubjectiveEl Constitucional — When Is the Electoral Debate Between Pedro S&aacute;nchez and Alberto N&uacute;&ntilde;ez Feij&oacute;oThe account carries the debate’s order: the encounter begins at 10 p.m. on Thursday, November 19, and is expected to last until midnight, with two three-minute commercial breaks; Mr. Feij&oacute;o will open the debate and Mr. S&aacute;nchez will have the last word, as decided by draw; and the five blocks run housing, the economy and taxation, social policy and public services, fighting corruption and democratic regeneration, and migration and foreign policy.

 SubjectiveDem&oacute;crata — General Election Poll: Vox Loses Four Seats and PP and PSOE Advance, According to 40dB TrackingThe account carries the November 18 instalment of the 40dB tracking for El Pa&iacute;s and Cadena SER: the Popular Party at 131 seats and the Socialists at 122, with Vox at 55; the Popular Party at 32.2 percent and the Socialists at 30.7; Mr. S&aacute;nchez remaining the preferred candidate to lead the government, ten points ahead of Mr. Feij&oacute;o; and the fieldwork, 2,000 online interviews from November 13 to 17, with a margin of error of 2.2 percent.

 SubjectiveDem&oacute;crata — Montero Attacks Face-to-Face S&aacute;nchez-Feij&oacute;oThe account carries the objection to tonight’s format: the Podemos candidate, Ms. Montero, described the head-to-head debate between Mr. S&aacute;nchez and Mr. Feij&oacute;o as “blackmail of the useful vote” and said neither of the blocs they head has any intention of making access to housing cheaper; and the survey of surveys at November 19, across 17 institutes, at 31.3 percent for the Popular Party, 27.5 for the Socialists and 19.0 for Vox.
